attributes.residual: REGISTER_ONLY, reduced to ONE named instruction. Target: `lwz r0,224(r28); cmpwi r0,25; mr r29,r0` - the loaded value is materialized in the scratch r0 for the compare and then COPIED into its callee-saved home r29. Ours: `lwz r29,224(r28); cmpwi r29,25` - MWCC coalesced the expression temp directly into the home and the copy disappears, leaving us exactly 1 instruction short (456 target / 455 ours) with an otherwise byte-aligned function. r29's other occupant is `data` (`addi r29,r30,4` @28), which is dead in this arm, so amount legitimately inherits r29 in BOTH builds - the ONLY divergence is whether the load targets r29 directly or transits r0. That is a coalescing cost decision inside MWCC's allocator with no source-level surface: it survived four assignment spellings and a scope change, and the one documented lever that could flip it (dead-local identity substitution) has no candidate carrier in this function. See claim.law.callee-saved-home-copy-coalescing-is-source-unreachable.20260831.v1, which generalizes this across three functions in this TU. Eligible for the WebFrank REGISTER_ONLY postprocessor path.
